gap: No result ChatGPT got states Samsung's own rule that Super Fast Charging switches on only if the bank supports USB PD PPS regardless of its wattage label, or Apple's spec that the iPhone 17's 50%-in-20-minutes needs a 40 W-or-higher PD source, which together set the real wattage a '45 W' 10,000 mAh bank delivers to each phone.
standout_why: Compared against Engadget (explains ~60% conversion efficiency and 10,000 mAh in = ~5,800 mAh out, mentions Qi2 25W for iPhone 17/Pixel 10 Pro XL, never mentions PPS or the 40 W threshold), the Anker blog (states 45 W Samsung / 40 W iPhone 17 for one product but never names PPS or the Apple adapter rule), and TechRadar (page body unreadable; title only). WSJ could not be opened. ChatGPT's answer itself says only 'USB-C PD, 20W or higher', which under Samsung's and Apple's rules fast-charges neither a Galaxy S25 at full speed nor an iPhone 17. New and useful; not a 3 because the capacity-loss half is already on Engadget and I could not read the Baseus AM52 spec sheet to confirm its PPS support.
decides: For a Samsung shopper the pick must list PPS or 'Samsung Super Fast Charging 2.0' in its protocol table, not just '45 W PD' (Anker Nano 10K A1638 does; INIU P41L-E2 lists PPS per search results but its page was unreachable; Baseus AM52 unconfirmed). For an iPhone 17 shopper the bank must negotiate 40 W or more over PD (Anker A1638 states 40 W for iPhone 17) or the 20-minute figure does not apply; 20-30 W banks drop to the slower tier. For either phone the 10,000 mAh label delivers roughly 5,800 mAh at the phone (Engadget), so ChatGPT's '1.5-2 charges' holds only for phones under ~3,700 mAh. The Qi2.2 25 W wireless mode on the Baseus PicoGo AM52 matches Apple's stated 25 W Qi2 ceiling for iPhone 17, which Anker's 15 W Qi2 MagGo picks do not reach.

findings.label: Super Fast Charging requires PPS
findings.value: USB PD PPS required; wattage alone does not enable it
findings.source_title: How to enable Fast charging and Fast wireless charging on your Samsung Galaxy phone
findings.note: Samsung page (Levant region, English, updated Oct 02, 2026) quote: 'Even if a charger has a high maximum output, Super fast charging may not be available if the charger does not support PPS.' Tiers on the page: 25 W EP-T2510 = Super fast charging; 45 W EP-T4511 = SFC 2.0 'based on use with a 45W, 5A cable'; 60 W EP-T6010 = SFC 3.0. 'For Galaxy S25 and later models, SFC 2.0 is supported when using the 3A USB cable included with the device.' No US-region page found stating the PPS rule.

findings.label: Which Galaxy models take 45 W (SFC 2.0)
findings.value: S24+, S24 Ultra, S25+, S25 Ultra, S26+, S26 Ultra; base S24/S25/S26, FE and Edge cap at 25 W; 60 W only S26 Ultra
findings.source_title: Which type of charger does my Galaxy device accept?
findings.note: Samsung UK compatibility chart, updated 29 October 2026. Super Fast Charging 25 W listed under 'USB-C Power Delivery (USB PD) with PPS'. Chart columns were flattened in the page text; ticks matched by column order. A 45 W bank is therefore only worth paying for with a Plus/Ultra Galaxy.

findings.label: Fast-charge threshold
findings.value: 50% in 20 min needs 40 W adapter or higher; 25 W MagSafe/Qi2 wireless needs 30 W or higher
findings.note: Exact lines: 'Up to 50% charge in 20 minutes with 40W adapter or higher (available separately) paired with USB-C charging cable'; 'Up to 50% charge in 30 minutes with 30W adapter or higher paired with MagSafe Charger'; 'MagSafe wireless charging up to 25W'; 'Qi2 wireless charging up to 25W'. Footnote 6: 25 W wireless 'with 30W power adapter or higher'; tests with drained units. ChatGPT's '20W or higher' advice does not meet this.
